html:
Anzac Day, 25 April, marks the landing of the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps at Gallipoli in Turkey in 1915. It was first held in 1916 and is the most important day of remembrance in Australia and New Zealand.

The campaign of World War I failed, and over 8,000 Australians and about 2,700 New Zealanders died there. Many saw in the soldiers' endurance the birth of a national spirit, the Anzac legend.

Dawn services began in the 1920s. The day now honours all who served, and crowds also visit the Australian War Memorial in Canberra and Anzac Cove itself. See New Zealand Wars for older wars.
